overview: Namibia's street food scene centers on informal open-air markets where vendors grill meat over open fires. The most famous specialty is kapana, strips of beef grilled to order and dipped in chili salt, best experienced at Windhoek's Oshetu Community Market. Visitors will also find vetkoek and dried mopane worms.
months: Summer brings intense heat and occasional heavy rains, which can make navigating unshaded outdoor markets challenging. The kapana grills remain active, and fresh mopane worms sometimes appear in northern markets toward the end of the rainy season.

overview: Raja Ampat is a remote island group with a basic food scene. Street food is limited to small local markets and modest stalls in the main town of Waisai, with simple Indonesian staples like nasi goreng, mie goreng, and grilled fish.
months: Waisai's small market and harbor area host a few stalls selling grilled fish, satay, and fried rice. The selection is modest, focusing on basic Indonesian comfort food for locals and travelers passing through to the islands.

overview: The Scottish Highlands and Isle of Skye feature a street food scene centered on fresh seafood and local game. Visitors find wooden shacks serving fresh langoustines and scallops right on the harbor in the warmer months, alongside monthly farmers' markets selling venison and haggis.
months: Most coastal food shacks close entirely for the winter. The Inverness Farmers' Market still operates on the first Saturday of the month, but outdoor eating is limited to a few hardy vendors selling hot Cullen skink or haggis.

overview: Tierra del Fuego has a modest street food scene centered around casual food trucks and local fairs in Ushuaia and Rio Grande. Visitors can find stalls serving choripán and baked empanadas. The outdoor eating culture is active in the warmer months when food trucks operate reliably near the ports.
months: Food trucks near the Ushuaia port and local fairs are fully operational. Visitors can grab choripán, empanadas, and hot chocolate to eat outside in the milder weather.

overview: Victoria Falls and the surrounding towns feature modest local markets where visitors can try Zimbabwean staples. Open-air stalls and community hubs like Chinotimba Market host vendors selling roasted corn, dried kapenta, and seasonal macimbi.
months: Summer rains occasionally disrupt open-air stalls, but this brings fresh seasonal foods. Vendors roast fresh corn on the cob over charcoal, and macimbi (mopane worms) appear in the markets after the heavy showers.
